Supported means the stated Rust contract has supplied code and named tests; it does not imply every official option or every engine release was exercised. Partial rows name the limits. Engine versions beside live tests identify executed proof targets; support floors are separately documented SDK requirements.

OpenTelemetry requires the `opentelemetry` Cargo feature (enabled by default) and an application-configured provider/exporter. Local transports do not emulate engine-owned guarantees.

Single/bulk HARD routing and eventual restart recovery verified for reconnecting/new workers and a workflow/action first created after restart on baseline/current engines. Observed recovery was ~61–63 seconds; original45-second failures are retained. TS1.43.0 submissions to the same Rust workers recovered in the same window. Fast recovery, worker-versus-engine attribution and latency SLA remain unproven. See batch-5.md. |

## Keeping references current

Run `python3 scripts/parity.py check-upstream` to detect changed releases or main. Run `refresh` to update the reference snapshot, inspect changed official implementations, then update feature rows and tests before claiming new support. `render --check` validates the matrix and deterministic Markdown without network access. CI checks the local matrix on changes; a separate scheduled/manual job detects upstream drift and uploads the observed versions. It never changes support claims automatically.

The baseline and current-release CI jobs execute the named Rust live suites against exact engine image digests. External official SDK source references establish the compared contract; these jobs do not execute the TS/Go SDK suites or establish all-language behavioral equivalence.
